content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, and built a limitation-by-limitation source ledger against the disclosure.

input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed. I traced every limitation of all seventeen claims (independent claims 1, 11 and 14 and dependent claims 2-10, 12-13 and 15-17), every one of the 28 entries in the numeral ledger (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48, 50, 52, 54, 56, 58, 60, 62, 64, 66), every structure, relationship, result, position, connection, operating condition and variant in the Field, Summary, Brief Description and Detailed Description, and every geometric statement in the FIG. 1-FIG. 4 briefs, back to affirmative passages in input/disclosure.md (the only inventor authority; the single USER passage in input/conversation.md is a truncated copy of the same text and adds nothing). The ledger closes: the two semicircular halves, hinge at one end and releasable latch at the other, three radial jaw carriages in radial guides, pivoting concave jaw pads that need no tool-specific pipe diameter, the segmented cam ring in an annular guide with one segment per frame half, complementary hinge-end and latch-end drive faces coupled by closure, follower-in-oblique-slot synchronization of all three carriages, the wedge bearing on a ring drive face, the limited stroke, outward carriage springs, the holding position and over-center position, the force-limiting spring stack between latch handle and wedge, the indicator pin reading against a fixed edge of the latch housing over a predetermined compression range, the express statement that the indicator does not measure pipe diameter, the optional mounting boss outside the annular guide that does not participate in jaw synchronization, and the install/remove sequences all rest on exact affirmative disclosure sentences. No unsupported material, result, dimension, angle, taper, contact topology or operating condition was found in the claims or description. The figure briefs stay within depiction convention: generic rectangles, the circle hinge, the zigzag spring, the schematic housing and the schematic end faces are marked "shown schematically", the functional faces (segment end faces, ring drive face, oblique slots, wedge) are described only in disclosed terms (matching/abutting outlines, inclination neither radial nor circumferential, common rotational sense entailed by the disclosed synchronized inward travel, drive face at the latch end entailed by the wedge being carried by the latch), and no depiction convention leaks into the application text - the description and Brief Description contain no "by way of example", "any closed outline", or other shape-justifying broadening, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question or unresolved alternative remains anywhere. Segment-to-half and end-to-end assignments are internally consistent across figures: 12 upper/16 hinge at the left break and 18 latch at the right break in FIG. 1, matching 32 upper segment with hinge-end face 44 and latch-end face 48 and 34 lower segment with 46 and 50 in FIG. 3, and matching the latch-end split under the housing in FIG. 4; three carriages/slots at top, lower left and lower right agree across FIGS. 1, 2 and 3; each numeral denotes exactly one part, every numeral used in the description appears in a figure brief and vice versa, and no section line is designated in any view, so there is no orphan section designation to reconcile. I noted, and confirmed as harmless, that the YOU passage in input/conversation.md claims the draft turns on a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface"; that is drafting-agent prose, is not inventor support, and correctly appears nowhere in the draft. Two verified internal inconsistencies remain, both minor and both fixable in the text alone: the description cross-references FIG. 2 for mounting boss 66 while the FIG. 2 brief deliberately leaves that projection unnumbered, and FIG. 3 is designated a "plan view" although it is taken along the same axis that FIGS. 1, 2 and 4 call a front elevation/front view. Per instruction I did not assess patentability, novelty, prior art in prior_art/, or rendered pixels; the brief itself records that no prior-art search was run, so the art on hand may be incomplete.

findings.title: Description cross-references FIG. 2 for mounting boss 66, but the FIG. 2 brief leaves that element unnumbered
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, section "The segmented cam ring"; figures/FIG-2.md (numerals list and Numeral placement targets)
findings.detail: The description directs the reader to FIG. 2 to see numeral 66, but the FIG. 2 brief neither lists 66 among its numerals nor gives it a placement target; it instead specifies the boss as an expressly unnumbered projection. A reader following the cross-reference finds no lead line or numeral 66 in that view. Numeral 66 is properly shown in FIG. 1, so this is a cross-reference defect rather than a missing-numeral defect, and the substantive relationship it states (boss outside the annular guide) is independently supported by the disclosure sentence "The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit", so no disclosure content is lost by correcting the reference.
findings.evidence: Description: "The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36, as shown in FIG. 2." FIG-2.md header: "numerals: [22, 24, 26, 30, 36, 38, 40, 42]" and geometry line: "An unnumbered small rectangular projection standing radially outward on the outer boundary circle at the upper right, radially outboard of the channel."
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md, delete the figure cross-reference so the sentence reads: "The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36." Make no change to figures/FIG-2.md. (Equivalent alternative, if the drawing is to carry the numeral: add 66 to the FIG. 2 numerals list and add the placement target "66: well inside the small rectangular projection at the upper right"; the text fix is preferred because it requires no drawing change.)

findings.title: FIG. 3 is designated a "plan view" although it is taken along the same axis that FIGS. 1, 2 and 4 designate a front view
findings.detail: FIG. 1 is designated a front elevation "along the pipe axis", FIG. 2 a "front interior view of the closed clamp along the pipe axis", and FIG. 4 is expressly "seen along the pipe axis as in FIG. 1". FIG. 3 shows the cam ring "viewed along its axis", and the cam ring axis is the central axis of the closed frame, i.e. the same viewing direction. Calling one view along that axis a plan view and the others front views is an inconsistent view designation across the set, and the Brief Description and the figure brief repeat the same inconsistent designation. No inventor-source or technical content is affected; only the view label needs to be harmonized.
findings.evidence: draft/07-drawings.md: "FIG. 3 is a plan view of the segmented cam ring alone..." versus "FIG. 1 is a front elevation of a split pipe clamp closed around a pipe" and "FIG. 2 is a front interior view of the closed split pipe clamp"; figures/FIG-3.md: "View: plan view of the cam ring alone, removed from the frame and viewed along its axis"; figures/FIG-4.md: "seen along the pipe axis as in FIG. 1".
findings.fix: Change the designation to a front view in both places. In draft/07-drawings.md: "FIG. 3 is a front view of the segmented cam ring alone, removed from the frame and laid out as it stands when the frame halves are closed." In figures/FIG-3.md, change the View line to: "View: front view of the cam ring alone, removed from the frame and viewed along its axis." Leave all geometry, numerals and placement targets unchanged.
